To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current Food and Drug Administration Bacteriological Analytic Manual method for the recovery of Salmonella Enteriditis from shell eggs can be improved by using tryptic soy broth as the preenrichent medium, and that surface disinfection of shell eggs prior to enrichment does not reduce the sensitivity to detection.

TSB is a suitable medium for preenrichement of Salmonella in egg samples and that egg:broth ratios and surface disinfection do not have a significant effect on the recovery of Salmonella Enterica from eggs.
TSB is the best preenrichment broth for the detection of SE in shell eggs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of Salmonellae in shell eggs.

the development and validation of a new method that will improve the sensitivity of detection, while simplifying the current Bacteriological Manual method for the isolation of Salmonella from shell eggs.
the improvement of the Food and Drug Administrations's Bacteriological Analytic Manual method for detection of Salmonella spp. in shell eggs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tryptic soy broths with 9:1 egg:broth ratio and surface disinfection with 70% isopropyl alcohol:iodine/ potassium iodide solution would be an improvement over the current method.
tryptic soy broths, egg:bacteriological analytical manual ratios at 1.5:1 or 1:1, and surface disinfectants did not affect the sensitivity of Salmonella Enteriditis detection in shell eggs.

the use of TSB as preenrichment broth, egg:broth ratios of 1:9 or 1:2, and no surface disinfection of shell eggs could improve the sensitivity of the current Bacteriological Manual method for the isolation of Salmonella Enteriditis in shell eggs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current Bacteriological Manual Method could be simplified by eliminating the use of Universal Preenrichent broth, and the use of nutrient broth and buffered peptones water, and changing to tryptic soy broth for preenrichent.
the use of tryptic soy broth for preenrichments and a 1:1 egg:preenriment broth ratio would be the best option for detecting Salmonella Enterititis in shell eggs.

the current Bacteriological Manual method can be improved to make it more effective and less expensive by using TSB, egg:broth ratio of 1:9 or 1:2, and no surface disinfection of eggs before preenrichment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of TSB as the preenrichement medium for shell eggs is a viable option for the detection of S. enterica ser. Enteritidis in the Bacteriological Analytic Manual (BAM).

TSB is a suitable medium for preenrichments of Salmonella Enteriditis in shell eggs and the use of 1:9 egg:broth ratio for preenriching Salmonella Enteritiditis in shell egg samples is more sensitive than 1:2 egg:broth.
the current Bacteriological Manual method can be modified and simplified without sacrificing the sensitivity of the method.
